1.name: Body
1.note: The cast housing. Its bore holds the oil and the piston, and its drillings carry the oil past the two needle valves.

2.name: End plug, spring side
2.note: Closes the bore at the spring end and gives the closing spring something to push against.

3.name: End plug, valve side
3.note: Closes the bore at the oil end, so oil can leave the pressure chamber only through the drillings beside it.

4.name: O-ring
4.note: Seals each end plug in the bore, so no oil escapes and the timing is set by the needles alone.

5.name: Piston with rack
5.note: Turns door motion into oil pressure. Opening the door drives it against the spring; the spring then drives it back, squeezing oil through the needles.

6.name: Piston ring
6.note: Seals the piston to the bore so the oil cannot slip past it. The only way out is the timed one, through the needles.

7.name: Closing spring
7.note: The energy source. It pushes the piston back and so shuts the door; the needles decide only how fast.

8.name: Pinion spindle
8.note: Meshes with the rack and carries the arm. It ties the door angle to the piston position, so every push moves the piston and restarts the closing.

9.name: Check ball
9.note: A one-way valve. Opening the door lifts it and the oil returns freely; closing seats it, so the oil must go through the needles.

10.name: Pin
10.note: Limits how far the check ball can lift, so it always drops back onto its seat.

11.name: Regulating screw 1, sweep
11.note: The sweep needle. Its setting is the orifice that sets how fast the door closes through most of its swing.

12.name: Regulating screw 2, latch
12.note: The latch needle. It alone passes oil near the end of the swing, so it sets the slower final closing into the latch.

13.name: O-ring
13.note: Seals the thread of each regulating screw, so the oil leaves only through the needle seat.

14.name: Sealing ball
14.note: Pressed in to plug the open end of a drilled oil passage.

15.name: Hydraulic oil
15.note: The working fluid. Its flow through the needles follows the orifice equation, which is what makes the closing time predictable.

16.name: Main arm
16.note: Joins the pinion spindle to the elbow, turning the door's swing into rotation of the spindle.

17.name: Forearm
17.note: Runs from the elbow to the shoe on the frame, so the arm folds and straightens as the door moves.

18.name: Arm shoe
18.note: The end of the forearm, bearing on the frame head.

19.name: Arm screw
19.note: Clamps the main arm onto the pinion spindle.

20.name: Elbow rivet
20.note: The hinge between the main arm and the forearm.

21.name: Door leaf
21.note: The door itself, shown for reference. Each push opens it, and that is the input the closer waits out.

22.name: Needle bearing
22.note: Carries the pinion spindle in the body so the spring force turns the arm with little friction.

23.name: Shaft seal
23.note: Keeps the oil in the body where the spindle leaves it.
